item.title: Lock, Stock and Two Tiled Fences: Haiku on a MacBook4,1
item.description:
On a MacBook4,1, Haiku showed a sliced desktop: skewed horizontal bands across the whole screen from boot onwards. It also showed no boot splash. Here is what was wrong, what changed, and why.

TL;DR
Hardware MacBook4,1, GMA X3100 (i965GM, 0x2a02, Gen4), LVDS on pipe B, Apple EFI 1.1 (UGA only, no GOP)
Symptom Sliced/skewed screen; no boot splash
Root cause Apple EFI leaves two X-tiled fences over aperture 0–32 MB. Haiku cleared fences on Gen6+ only, so every linear CPU write to our frame buffer got tiled on the way in.
Fix Clear the 16 fences on Gen4–5 before the first mode set
Bonus fixes Plane/pipe hygiene on Gen ≤4, the GTT location and entry count in intel_gart, a missing &, and a boot splash on GOP-less Intel EFI

Tested on one MacBook4,1 only. See Testing wanted.

item.title: World Around Us
item.description: We live in world, but what does world means to us? The surrounding reality? These are value judgments only. We live on planet Earth and this is our world. Humanity has expanded its habitat, agriculture, electricity transport are the achievements of modern mankind. A industrialized society can manage living conditions. But have we solved all problems? There is a world around us and there is garbage, destruction of natural resources. People began to think they on their own, the crown of evolution. But how many people can survive in the forest without technology? The truth is that we are part of the system, ecosystem, part of nature. And we are completely dependent on nature well-being.

item.title: Udev Device Mapping for Daily Tasks
item.description:
Does USB device should always have specific access rights? Or network cards must have specific names? For such questions, and even more, Linux has a standard tool in its arsenal – UDEV. UDEV is a userspace system that allows you to identify devices based on their properties, and register userspace handlers.

Set persistent name for device.
